description: The ONNX pair that was found at server/model.onnx (written 2026-05-15), relocated here unmodified and addressed by content. Identity is known and verified; provenance is NOT, and was never recoverable. This manifest records what these bytes ARE. It deliberately records nothing about how they perform or whether they are in use, because those change without these bytes changing. See docs/superpowers/2026-08-06-model-path-provenance-audit.md and docs/superpowers/2026-08-13-product-model-alignment-decision-memo.md.
model_id_note: The id is sha256(graph_sha256 + ':' + external_data_sha256), first 16 hex. It addresses the PAIR. An id derived from the graph alone would collide across models whose topology and external-data filenames match, which is every export of this architecture.
provenance_note: Every provenance field is unknown and must not be reconstructed or guessed. The audit established conclusively that this artifact did NOT come from calib020_0001: the ONNX was written 2026-05-15, five weeks before that checkpoint existed. It could not positively identify the source. checkpoints/alphazero-v2-staged/model_iter_0193.safetensors is circumstantial only, on timestamp-plus-mechanism evidence, and is deliberately NOT recorded above as fact. The graph carries no metadata_props and no doc_string, and the file was untracked, so no record survives. Future candidate manifests, produced by a known export, must populate every field completely.
contract_note: Enforced at startup three ways, not merely recorded: against onnxruntime-node session metadata; for internal consistency, so board_shape and max_moves must follow from the declared tensors; and against the fixed application contract this server can actually consume, derived from gameLogic NUM_CHANNELS and BOARD_SIZE plus AlphaZeroInference.maxMoves. The third matters because a model and a manifest that agree with each other can still describe an interface the server cannot feed or read - a 24-channel board, or an output named score - and mutual agreement would otherwise let it through. Measured from this artifact: 76 nodes, 53 initializers of which 33 carry external data, every external-data location equal to "model.onnx.data". BatchNorm is folded into the convolutions - 0 BatchNormalization ops against Relu 16, Conv 14, Slice 8, Add 6, Concat 4, Where 4, Gemm 4.
claims: Identity only. This manifest asserts that model.onnx and model.onnx.data are the bytes described by graph, external_data and contract, and nothing more. Provenance is unknown in every field and must not be reconstructed or guessed. It makes NO parity, strength, serving-status or deployment-status claim of its own. Those are properties of a programme and of a deployment rather than of an artifact: they change while these bytes stay identical, so a manifest that encoded them would go stale silently and without any signal. Model selection is determined by repository and deployment configuration; this manifest does not determine it, and what is actually running is a fact about a deployment rather than about this file. The separately reviewed records own those conclusions: provenance audit, docs/superpowers/2026-08-06-model-path-provenance-audit.md; product-stack comparison, in which this pair was the baseline arm, docs/superpowers/2026-08-14-product-stack-comparison-specification.md with evidence under tests/product_match/match/aca5ca2/; served-default switch, docs/superpowers/2026-08-22-default-model-switch.md.
